items.headline: BMW first carmaker to integrate Alexa+ LLM assistant, starting iX3
items.driver: BMW expands its Intelligent Personal Assistant on Amazon's Alexa+ architecture; first public demo at CES 2026; iX3 customers in DE and US first from H2 2026.
items.customer_relevance: Natural, multi-part voice dialogue becomes a premium baseline expectation; successors on OS 9/X should get it via OTA.
items.quote: BMW will become the first car manufacturer to integrate the AI assistant technology into its vehicles ... Starting in the second half of 2026, BMW iX3 customers in Germany and the US will be the first
items.notes: Footnote: all BMW models with Operating System 9 and X to receive it gradually, at the latest in H2 2026. No verified source found on actual rollout/reception by 2026-07-31.

items.headline: BMW LLM assistant handles multiple questions in one sentence
items.driver: Shown at CES 2026; LLM lets the assistant answer complex questions mixing vehicle functions and general knowledge.
items.customer_relevance: Customers may stop accepting fixed voice-command lists; conversational control of car functions becomes a differentiator.
items.quote: will be able to ask multiple questions in a single sentence ... The car will understand complex questions and provide appropriate answers.
items.notes: Example wake phrase 'Hey BMW'. No customer reception data.

items.headline: Mercedes MBUX Virtual Assistant built on Google Gemini, CLA first
items.driver: Partnership with Google Cloud's Automotive AI Agent integrated with Google Maps; CLA debuts MB.OS.
items.customer_relevance: Competitors pair LLM assistants with rich POI/navigation data; BMW assistant must match conversational navigation quality.
items.quote: powered by Google Cloud's new Automotive AI Agent and integrated into Google Maps ... will be the first Mercedes-Benz model to feature the Automotive AI Agent.
items.notes: Existing MBUX also uses ChatGPT and Bing results (secondary reports).

items.headline: S-Class facelift adds generative-AI MBUX ('Hey Mercedes' ChatGPT)
items.driver: Mercedes facelift unveiled late January 2026 integrates generative AI into MBUX.
items.customer_relevance: In the 7 Series' direct rival, conversational GenAI is now standard luxury content.
items.quote: The latest MBUX system now integrates generative AI.
items.notes: Other outlets (not fetched) say MBUX combines ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Microsoft Bing. Same reveal also removed Drive Pilot L3 (see mercedes-drive-pilot-paused). Published 2026-01-30, inside the 2026-01 cut-off.

items.headline: S-Class grille grows ~20% and is illuminated for first time
items.driver: Facelift design update; grille larger and lit, with 3D chrome star elements.
items.customer_relevance: Luxury rivals use bigger, lit front signatures for presence; 7 Series successor design must hold its own visually in CN/US.
items.quote: The front grille is now around 20 percent larger and, for the first time, illuminated
items.notes: Contrasts with BMW Neue Klasse move to smaller kidneys.

items.headline: BMW shrinks kidney grille, integrates lighting in Neue Klasse iX3
items.driver: Per the source, BMW designers heard complaints about the grille; iX3 kidney is smaller with headlights illuminated within it.
items.customer_relevance: Signals that grille-size backlash mattered; successors should avoid oversized-grille polarisation while keeping recognisable kidney.
items.quote: the kidney grilles are getting smaller ... illuminated directly within the front grille, creating the illusion of an infinity effect.
items.notes: Source also notes haptic touch-sensitive steering wheel controls ('shy-tech').

items.headline: 7 Series/i7 facelift brings Panoramic iDrive and revised lit kidney
items.driver: Facelift of G70 (still CLAR) adopts Neue Klasse tech: full-width Panoramic display, OS X, revised illuminated kidney; production from July at Dingolfing.
items.customer_relevance: Neue Klasse HMI is spreading into CLAR luxury cars; G70 successor baseline now includes it.
items.quote: BMW 7 Series facelift debuts with Neue Klasse tech, fresh design and EV range boost
items.notes: Page returned 403; details from search snippets (17.9-inch central screen, 14.6-inch passenger display, revealed in New York). Verify against BMW PressClub. Model year labelled 2026 or 2027 by different outlets.

items.headline: Tesla ships Grok chatbot in new cars from July 2025
items.driver: Grok beta on AMD-infotainment Teslas; conversational, selectable personalities; could not control car functions yet.
items.customer_relevance: LLM chat in cars is arriving fast via OTA; premium buyers will compare depth of car-function control, not just chat.
items.quote: all new vehicles delivered on or after July 12, 2025, will include Grok AI out of the box ... Grok cannot currently issue commands to the vehicle itself.
items.notes: Requires Premium Connectivity or Wi-Fi.

items.headline: Tesla launches Grok in nine European markets incl. Germany
items.driver: Announced 16 Feb 2026; real-time answers and navigation editing; EU investigation of Grok content safety noted.
items.customer_relevance: European buyers now experience LLM assistants in cars; privacy/content-safety concerns are part of acceptance.
items.quote: initially covering the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Italy, France, Portugal, and Spain
items.notes: A T3 source (basenor, 2026-07-21) reports Grok 'now available in all of Europe' with the 2026 Summer Update.

items.headline: Grok available across all of Europe with Summer Update
items.driver: Tesla Europe post cited by blog; part of 2026 Summer Update.
items.customer_relevance: In-car LLM assistant becoming ubiquitous at a mass-premium rival in Europe by mid-2026.
items.quote: Also, Grok now available in all of Europe.
items.notes: Low-tier source quoting a Tesla Europe post; not corroborated by T1/T2.

items.headline: Chinese brands rush DeepSeek LLM into smart cockpits
items.driver: Geely (6 Feb), Baojun and IM Motors (8 Feb 2025) announced DeepSeek integration; IM also works with Doubao and Tongyi models.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese premium buyers expect locally-tuned LLM assistants; BMW China cockpits need comparable domestic AI partners.
items.quote: integration of the DeepSeek R1 large language model in its Lingyu Smart Cockpit has been completed.
items.notes: Dongfeng also announced lineup-wide DeepSeek integration (Gasgoo, Feb 2025; page 403). Doubao usage figure '7M+ cars, 145 models' seen only in an undated secondary summary - not recorded.

items.headline: Euro NCAP 2026 rewards physical controls for common functions
items.driver: Euro NCAP 2026 protocols (announced 26 Nov 2025) introduce HMI assessments of intuitiveness of controls.
items.customer_relevance: Physical controls for core functions become rating-relevant in Europe; touch-only interiors risk safety score and customer criticism.
items.quote: cars will be scored on how intuitive their controls are ... for commonly used functions such as climate control will earn manufacturers extra points.
items.notes: Euro NCAP's own release (euroncap.com, 2025-11-26) body not retrievable. Sources disagree on whether buttons are a hard gate for 5 stars (ETSC) or point-earning (Carwow).

items.headline: ETSC: top Euro NCAP rating needs physical controls for core functions
items.driver: Euro NCAP pushes back against touchscreen-only interiors: indicators, hazards, wipers, horn, SOS/eCall need dedicated physical controls.
items.customer_relevance: Core driving controls should stay physical on successors; minimalism must not remove them.
items.quote: To secure a top safety rating, manufacturers must provide dedicated physical controls for core functions
items.notes: Conflicts in strictness with Carwow description (points vs. requirement).

items.headline: Euro NCAP 2026: 5 stars need continuous eye/head tracking
items.driver: Euro NCAP emphasises Driver State Monitoring against distraction and impairment.
items.customer_relevance: Interior cameras become standard; customers will judge how intrusive or helpful monitoring alerts feel.
items.quote: To achieve a 5-star rating, vehicles must employ continuous eye- and head-tracking.
items.notes: J.D. Power IQS 2026: 18% of distraction complaints come from driver-assistance alerts.

items.headline: ANCAP follows Euro NCAP in scoring physical buttons from 2026
items.driver: ANCAP: physical buttons or stalks for key controls encouraged through scoring, mirroring Euro NCAP HMI assessment.
items.customer_relevance: Button-friendly HMI becoming a multi-market safety-rating norm, not just a European one.
items.quote: Physical buttons or stalks to operate these key vehicle controls will be encouraged through scoring
items.notes: Quote from ANCAP CEO Carla Hoorweg. Australia is outside BMW focus regions; listed as GLOBAL spread signal.

items.headline: VW ID. Polo brings back physical buttons after ID.3 criticism
items.driver: Criticism of touch-heavy ID.3 cabin forced VW to restore physical switchgear.
items.customer_relevance: Mass brands reverting signals broad buyer preference; premium touch-only controls look out of step.
items.quote: A lot of criticism followed, forcing VW to not only bring back physical switchgear
items.notes: Other reports (not fetched) say VW described the interior as 'systematically optimised based on customer feedback' and that future ID models follow.

items.headline: Mercedes CEO: industry went too far, sensible buttons return
items.driver: Källenius (to Autocar) says technology for its own sake forgot the customer; screens stay but sensible buttons come back.
items.customer_relevance: Premium leader now validates button demand; BMW successors should keep/expand haptic physical controls alongside screens.
items.quote: So from now on, you will see us reintroduce the most sensible buttons. ... I don't know if we're at peak screen, but we're at low button.
items.notes: Published on the cut-off day (2026-07-31). Mercedes had not formally announced the strategy on official channels per secondary coverage.

items.headline: 60% of UK drivers put off by touch-first controls (What Car?)
items.driver: What Car? survey of 1,428 motorists; nearly 90% prefer physical buttons.
items.customer_relevance: Touch-heavy HMI can cost conquest sales in UK/EU.
items.quote: Out of the 1,428 motorists surveyed by What Car?, 60 per cent would be put off buying a car that prioritised touch-sensitive buttons over physical ones.
items.notes: Page returned 403; quote from search snippet. Older study (2024) but was what a PM could know at Jan 2026.

items.headline: 47% of UK drivers say touchscreens make driving more distracting
items.driver: Quotezone survey; 31% feel screens are too big; 53% back restrictions on functions.
items.customer_relevance: Screen size growth has diminishing returns; physical controls and restraint in screen use may be valued.
items.quote: almost half (47%) of UK drivers believe touchscreen dashboards make driving more distracting
items.notes: Sample size not stated. Different question from What Car? item; compare direction only.

items.headline: 48% globally prefer touchscreen plus physical buttons/knobs
items.driver: S&P Global Mobility HMI consumer analysis.
items.customer_relevance: Hybrid HMI (screen + buttons) is the plurality preference; supports keeping iDrive controller/haptic keys.
items.quote: Nearly half (48%) of global respondents prefer a combination of touchscreens with physical buttons or knobs.
items.notes: Page returned 403; quote from search snippet. Exact publish day unknown (URL path 2026/02).

items.headline: J.D. Power IQS 2026: quality improves, infotainment only category worse
items.driver: Problems fell to 175 PP100 from 192; infotainment rose, driven largely by Android Auto/CarPlay connectivity issues.
items.customer_relevance: Smartphone integration reliability is a top quality pain point; premium successors need robust wireless CarPlay/Android Auto.
items.quote: driven largely by Android Auto/Apple CarPlay connectivity issues
items.notes: Value is PP100 (lower is better); yoy computed from 192 -> 175. J.D. Power press release (2026-06-25) returned 403. No IQS 2025 counterpart fetched.

items.headline: 46% of distraction complaints tied to infotainment/touchscreens
items.driver: J.D. Power IQS 2026; 18% from driver-assistance alerts.
items.customer_relevance: Touchscreen-centric HMI and nagging ADAS alerts are perceived distraction sources; design for glanceable, calm HMI.
items.quote: 46% of distracted-driving complaints were related to infotainment systems and touchscreens
items.notes: Share among owners who reported a distraction-related problem, not all owners.

items.headline: TXI 2025: touchless/hidden controls and biometrics generate many problems
items.driver: J.D. Power 2025 Tech Experience Index: biometric authentication 29.2 PP100, touchless/hidden controls 19.6, driver monitoring 19.4.
items.customer_relevance: Hidden/shy-tech controls frustrate owners; minimalist interiors need discoverability.
items.quote: Biometric authentication has 29.2 problems per 100 vehicles. Touchless or hidden controls have 19.6, and direct driver monitoring has 19.4.
items.notes: Quote is the fetch tool's rendering of the page; value in PP100. Premium innovation rank: Genesis 538, Cadillac 526, Lincoln 523.

items.headline: 62% of US owners want in-vehicle payments
items.driver: J.D. Power TXI 2025: charging, fuel, parking and tolls most common uses; car-wash mode usability issues (38% want better instructions).
items.customer_relevance: Integrated payment for charging/parking is a wanted connected service in the US.
items.quote: 62% of owners want the feature. Charging, fuel, parking, and tolls are the most common uses.
items.notes: Quote is the fetch tool's rendering of the page.

items.headline: BMW gets UN R171 approval: hands-off up to 130 km/h across Europe
items.driver: First carmaker in Germany with international DCAS approval; glance-confirmed lane change; iX3 launch markets DE, AT, IT, FR, BE, NL, LU, CH, LI.
items.customer_relevance: Hands-off motorway driving becomes expected in EU premium; successors need it across markets, with glance-based lane changes.
items.quote: take their hands off the wheel for longer periods at speeds of up to 130 km/h ... All the driver needs to do is confirm the proposed manoeuvre by glancing in the wing mirror.
items.notes: Unit km refers to km/h speed limit. City functions (stopping at red lights) promised via OTA per secondary sources.

items.headline: Tesla says RDW committed to FSD approval in Feb 2026
items.driver: Tesla strategy centred on Dutch RDW national approval.
items.customer_relevance: Point-to-point supervised L2 may reach Europe; raises bar for BMW assistance scope.
items.quote: Currently, RDW has committed to granting Netherlands National approval in February 2026
items.notes: Tesla's claim; actual approval came April 2026.

items.headline: Netherlands RDW grants first European FSD (Supervised) approval
items.driver: Type approval as L2 ADAS under UN R171; other states may adopt; Denmark provisional authorisation by June.
items.customer_relevance: European premium buyers can now compare city/urban supervised assistance; BMW's Motorway/City Assistant faces direct benchmark.
items.quote: Tesla has received the first approval for its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system in Europe from the Dutch authority RDW.
items.notes: Updated 2026-06-15: Denmark authorisation provisional pending European Commission approval.

items.headline: Mercedes drops L3 Drive Pilot from S-Class facelift, goes L2++
items.driver: Per Handelsblatt: L2 avoids expensive lidar, cutting cost; replaced by MB.Drive Assist Pro (L2++ with navigation).
items.customer_relevance: Eyes-off L3 had limited customer value vs. cost; broad hands-off L2++ with navigation is what luxury buyers get.
items.quote: the new version will likely only feature a Level 2 system instead.
items.notes: Drive Pilot had German approval for 95 km/h since Dec 2024 (not fetched). Sources differ: 'pause' vs 'discontinued'. EQS facelift reportedly also excludes it.

items.headline: China approves first two L3 passenger cars (Changan, Arcfox)
items.driver: MIIT market access: Changan up to 50 km/h in congestion, Arcfox up to 80 km/h, single lane, designated roads in Chongqing and Beijing.
items.customer_relevance: L3 arrives in China in narrow use cases; Chinese premium buyers may expect eyes-off congestion assist on successors.
items.quote: The first approved model is Changan's SC7000AAARBEV pure electric sedan.
items.notes: Value = max speed km/h (Arcfox). Pilot use only.

items.headline: China L3 pilot: liability can shift to OEM and supplier
items.driver: China Daily on L3 pilots in Beijing and Chongqing; driver only needs to respond to takeover requests.
items.customer_relevance: Liability clarity makes eyes-off time usable (rear-seat style comfort for driver); trust driver for adoption.
items.quote: the responsibility for the driving task can be allocated among the driver, the car manufacturer and the system supplier

items.headline: China L2 ADAS penetration 70.5% in H1 2026; L3 cars on roads
items.driver: Beijing reached 77.5% L2 penetration vs 70.5% national; first L3 vehicles already operating on public roads.
items.customer_relevance: L2 is now near-universal in new Chinese cars; L2 is hygiene, differentiation moves to NOA/L3.
items.quote: reached 77.5%, surpassing the national average of 70.5% for the same period
items.notes: Primary data source not named. Same article: 'The first batch of conditionally automated L3-level vehicles has already begun operating on public roads'.

items.headline: Urban NOA in 15.1% of China's insured new cars (Jan–Nov 2025)
items.driver: CAAM City NOA report: 3.129m units, +5.6 pp vs 2024; under RMB 300k, City NOA models >68.9% of sales (per source).
items.customer_relevance: City point-to-point assistance is going mainstream in China; a premium successor without it will look behind.
items.quote: cumulative sales of passenger vehicles equipped with City NOA in China reached 3.129 million units ... a 15.1% penetration rate of insured passenger vehicles
items.notes: Conflicts: GGII 15.18% (2.07m, pre-installed, CarNewsChina 2026-02-01); New Energy Outlook 11.6% (2.67m newly insured, full 2025, 36kr 2026-04-13). 68.9% is share within <RMB300k band as phrased by source (ambiguous).

items.headline: Chinese brands hold 81.1% of urban NOA cars; Momenta+Huawei ~80%
items.driver: CAAM report: domestic brands 2.5373m units; Momenta and Huawei dominate supplier market.
items.customer_relevance: Foreign premium brands lag in China smart driving; BMW China needs a competitive local NOA stack.
items.quote: domestic brands accounted for 2.5373 million units, or a remarkable 81.1% share
items.notes: China Daily (2026-02-16) says Momenta+Huawei ~80% of the third-party urban NOA market.

items.headline: GGII: urban NOA pre-installs 2.07m in 2025, +156%
items.driver: Factory-installed urban NOA, excluding imports/exports.
items.customer_relevance: Confirms ~15% full-year penetration; urban NOA growth is steep.
items.quote: 2.0709 million units, a year-on-year increase of 155.83% ... with a penetration rate of 15.18%
items.notes: yoy_pct refers to units. Published Feb 1 so belongs to 2026-07 checkpoint though it covers FY2025. Another source gives 11.6% (newly insured basis).

items.headline: Alternative count: urban NOA 11.6% of newly insured cars 2025
items.driver: 2.67m newly insured vehicles with urban NOA; L2 expected to exceed 70% penetration in 2026.
items.customer_relevance: Even conservative counts show >1 in 10 new Chinese cars with city NOA.
items.quote: reached 2.67 million, accounting for 11.6% of the total number of newly insured domestic passenger cars
items.notes: Conflicts with CAAM 15.1% (Jan–Nov) and GGII 15.18%; differing bases.

items.headline: NOA-equipped cars reach 34.2% of China passenger vehicles in H1 2026
items.driver: Nationwide NOA (highway + urban) penetration; source does not name data provider.
items.customer_relevance: Navigation-based assisted driving becoming majority-adjacent in China; table stakes for premium within successor horizon.
items.quote: the nationwide penetration rate of Navigation on Autopilot (NOA)-equipped passenger vehicles stood at 34.2%
items.notes: Definition differs from pair (all NOA vs urban NOA only) - not directly comparable to 15.1%.

items.headline: Factory NOA deliveries +51% in H1 2026 despite weak market
items.driver: Intelligent-driving domain controllers reached 3.1732m units, 37.21% penetration; total domestic PV deliveries fell (per secondary summary ~20%).
items.customer_relevance: Buyers are shifting to NOA-equipped cars even in a falling market; smart driving is a purchase driver in China.
items.quote: Deliveries of models with factory-installed NOA surged by 51.23% year-over-year ... a penetration rate of 37.21%
items.notes: 37.21% refers to domain controllers, not NOA. Data source not named.

items.headline: Huawei expects 80+ models with Qiankun ADS by end 2026
items.driver: Huawei's Jin Yuzhi (mid-January); urban NOA moving from high-end to mainstream; cumulative 3m installs projected.
items.customer_relevance: Huawei-powered rivals set Chinese premium expectations for smart driving above RMB 200k.
items.quote: by the end of 2026, more than 80 models are expected to be equipped with Huawei's Qiankun driving assistance system
items.notes: Value = number of models (unit none).

items.headline: China bans 'autonomous/intelligent driving' wording after Xiaomi SU7 crash
items.driver: MIIT meeting after fatal March 2025 crash: must say 'L-level assisted driving'; no unsupervised parking/summon; DMS cannot be disabled; OTA only after validation.
items.customer_relevance: China buyers will see honest, level-labelled ADAS; BMW China comms and features (remote parking) must fit these limits.
items.quote: over-the-air updates can only be transmitted after validation has been completed.
items.notes: Based on reported meeting minutes, not official MIIT text.

items.headline: China tightens OTA: record updates, notify users, no beta systems
items.driver: MIIT 1 March 2025 circular on market access, recalls and OTA; ADAS crackdown after late-March crash.
items.customer_relevance: Fewer, validated OTA feature drops in China; customers get clearer update notices.
items.quote: prohibit car companies from releasing unfinished or actively updating systems.
items.notes: No verified 2026-07 follow-up (e.g. mandatory L2 standard, concealed door handle ban) - search budget exhausted.

items.headline: Super Cruise passes 1 billion hands-free miles, ~750k cars
items.driver: GM: nearly 750,000 Super Cruise-enabled vehicles across 23 models in North America; eyes-off on Escalade IQ in 2028.
items.customer_relevance: Hands-free highway driving is mainstream in US luxury; BMW US successors must match coverage and availability.
items.quote: nearly 750,000 Super Cruise-enabled vehicles ... across 23 models in North America ... eyes-off driving on the Cadillac ESCALADE IQ in 2028
items.notes: Vehicle count includes free-trial users, not paying subscribers. GM's own release (news.gm.com 2026-04-28) returned 403.

items.headline: BYD introduced 1,000 kW megawatt charging in March 2025
items.driver: 1,000 V platform, 10C charging rates.
items.customer_relevance: In China, 5-minute 'refuel-like' charging resets expectations for BEV charging time.
items.quote: was introduced in March 2025 ... provided a peak output of 1,000 kW and supported 10C charging rates on 1,000V platforms
items.notes: Event public March 2025; page version retrieved 2026-10 (published_at unknown). Replace with a dated T2 source if possible.

items.headline: BYD begins large-scale megawatt flash-charging deployment
items.driver: Plans 4,000+ own sites plus 10,000 with Xiaoju and 5,000 with LongShine; second-gen up to 2,100 kW reported.
items.customer_relevance: Ultra-fast charging infrastructure scaling in China raises charging-time expectations for premium BEVs.
items.quote: jointly build 10,000 1-MW charging stations with Xiaoju and 5,000 with LongShine
items.notes: Wikipedia says the 1,500 kW 2026 system was introduced 5 March 2026.

items.headline: BYD reaches 5,000 flash stations in 27 days; 10–70% in ~5 min
items.driver: Network in 297 cities; target 20,000 by end 2026; at −30 °C 20–97% about 12 minutes.
items.customer_relevance: Real cold-weather fast charging is being demonstrated; winter charging performance becomes a comparison point.
items.quote: 10 % to 70 % in around 5 minutes ... establishing 20,000 flash stations nationwide by the end of 2026
items.notes: By late May >6,100 China stations (CarNewsChina 2026-06-09).

items.headline: BYD opens first 1,500 kW flash charger in Germany
items.driver: Plans 6,000 flash stations outside China by end 2026, half in Europe; >6,100 in China by late May.
items.customer_relevance: Megawatt charging becomes visible to German buyers; BMW BEV charging speed will be compared directly.
items.quote: BYD plans to build 6,000 flash-charging stations outside China by the end of 2026
items.notes: Only BYD's own compatible vehicles benefit.

items.headline: 800V cars 6.9% of China sales in 2024, 9.5% forecast 2025
items.driver: 800V models rose from 13 (2022) to 70+ by mid-2025, now down to RMB 100–150k price points.
items.customer_relevance: Fast charging via 800V is spreading to mass prices; premium buyers will expect it as standard.
items.quote: 840,000 units in 2024 ... 6.9% market penetration ... projected to hit 9.5% in 2025
items.notes: 2025 figure is a forecast; no 2026 actual found. Base (all PV vs NEV) unclear.

items.headline: BMW EVs gain US Tesla Supercharger access from Dec 10, 2025
items.driver: Official adapters only from Q2 2026; native NACS starting with 2026 i5 M60; some 2026 i5/iX need spring 2026 software update.
items.customer_relevance: US charging experience improves; native port and in-nav Supercharger routing become expected on successors.
items.quote: Starting December 10, 2025, drivers of electric BMWs finally have access to the expansive Tesla Supercharger network.
items.notes: BMW lagged Mercedes (access Feb 2025, secondary source). No 2026-07 follow-up verified.

items.headline: Ionna (BMW co-owned) targeted 100 stations / 1,000 bays by end-2025
items.driver: Goal set February 2025; 30,000 charge points by 2030.
items.customer_relevance: OEM-backed premium charging network promises better US charging experience for BMW drivers.
items.quote: a secondary goal of 100 stations (1,000 charge points) by the end of 2025
items.notes: Target, not an actual count; no Jan-2026 actual found. Page version retrieved 2026-10.

items.headline: Ionna at 107 stations / 1,020 stalls by April 2026
items.driver: Network build-out; Axios (2026-07-08, not fetched) reports 120 Rechargery locations in 31 states and 60 under construction.
items.customer_relevance: US fast-charging coverage with lounge-style sites is growing but still small vs Tesla.
items.quote: As of April 2026 Ionna has 107 stations opened with 1020 stalls.
items.notes: published_at = date of the count stated on page. Axios July figure (120 sites) unverified (403).

items.headline: NAF winter test: Lucid Air 520 km at −31 °C, Mercedes CLA 421 km
items.driver: Coldest NAF test on record in Norway; results from Lucid press material.
items.customer_relevance: Winter range is a visible comparison; CLA (premium rival) performs strongly, raising bar for 5 Series/i5 successor.
items.quote: the next closest competitor, the Mercedes-Benz CLA, managed 421 km (261 miles)
items.notes: Norway (EEA, not EU); region tagged EU for European relevance. No BMW result found.

items.headline: 24 EVs lost 38% vs WLTP on average at −32 °C
items.driver: NAF El Prix winter test in Folldal, Norway.
items.customer_relevance: Real winter range is far below WLTP; Nordic/North China/US-north buyers need efficient heat pumps and honest range display.
items.quote: a 38% reduction
items.notes: Same test as Jan item; this aggregate figure was published after Jan cut-off.

items.headline: US EV share record 10.5% in Q3 2025 before credit expiry
items.driver: Pull-forward before federal EV tax credit expired 30 Sep 2025; 438,487 units.
items.customer_relevance: US BEV demand was incentive-driven; without credit, PHEV/ICE options matter more for US successors.
items.quote: electric cars accounted for 10.5 per cent of total car sales in the US

items.headline: US EV share falls to 5.8% in Q4 2025 after credit ends
items.driver: Post-credit plunge: 234,000 units, −46% QoQ, −36% YoY; FY2025 share 7.8%; Cox expected ~8% in 2026.
items.customer_relevance: US BEV appetite soft; successors need flexible powertrain offer in US.
items.quote: total EV sales in Q4 plunged to 234,000 units ... then fell to 5.8% in Q4
items.notes: yoy_pct refers to units. CarEdge reports 5.7%.

items.headline: US EV share stuck at ~5.8% in Q2 2026; hybrids forecast +9%
items.driver: 247,226 EVs (KBB est.), −20.5% YoY, +14.7% vs Q1; hybrid sales forecast to rise ~9%.
items.customer_relevance: Cox's ~8% 2026 outlook from January not met by mid-year; US buyers favour hybrids—PHEV/HEV variants matter for US derivatives.
items.quote: EV sales accounted for approximately 5.8% of total new-vehicle volume in the second quarter.
items.notes: yoy_pct refers to units. Hybrid +9% forecast phrased by fetch tool as 'first half of 2026'; search snippet said 'in 2026' - ambiguous.

items.headline: EU proposes 90% 2035 CO2 target; PHEVs, EREVs may stay
items.driver: Commission Automotive Package: remaining 10% offset via EU low-carbon steel, e-fuels, biofuels; new small-EV category up to 4.2 m.
items.customer_relevance: PHEV/EREV variants remain viable in Europe beyond 2035; customers keep powertrain choice.
items.quote: plug-in hybrids, range extenders, mild hybrids, and internal combustion engine vehicles can continue to be sold beyond 2035
items.notes: Proposal, not adopted law; status by 2026-07 not verified.

items.headline: China EREV sales fall three months running as BEVs improve
items.driver: New BEVs average >500 km range; 12.82m chargers end-2024; cheaper batteries. Li Auto down five months.
items.customer_relevance: In China, range anxiety fading as BEV range and charging improve; EREV appeal declining for premium.
items.quote: The average range of newly launched EVs in 2025 exceeds 500 km
items.notes: Value = Sep 2025 domestic EREV sales, yoy −13%. Share rose 3.6% (2021) to 9.1% (2024).

items.headline: China EREV sales topped 1.2m in 2025; stricter EREV standard coming
items.driver: New QC/T1086-2026 range-extender standard effective 1 Nov 2026 (durability, generator control).
items.customer_relevance: EREV still large in China; LWB/rear-comfort buyers may value long-range EREV, but momentum is slowing.
items.quote: surpassing 1.2 million units in 2025
items.notes: Value is 'over 1.2m' (lower bound). Secondary summaries cite CPCA May 2026 EREV wholesale 95,000 (−24.9% YoY) - not fetched.

items.headline: Huawei/JAC Maextro S800 sets Chinese rear-seat luxury benchmark
items.driver: Zero-gravity rear seats (20-way, 148.5° recline), massage, privacy screen partition, fridge; BEV and EREV.
items.customer_relevance: China LWB buyers benchmark rear lounge comfort against domestic rivals; relevant for G68/G70 successors.
items.quote: zero-gravity seats with 20-way electric adjustment, up to 148.5° recline
items.notes: Price range 708,000–1,018,000 CNY.

items.headline: Maextro S800 ~2,600 sales in Jan 2026, ~2x Maybach S / 7 Series
items.driver: Price and technology vs Maybach/Panamera; 14,000+ cumulative since mid-2025 debut.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese luxury buyers accept a domestic tech-led rear-seat flagship; 7 Series China positioning is under pressure.
items.quote: Tylko w styczniu 2026 roku Maextro S800 znalazł ponad 2600 nabywców ... Mercedes-Maybach klasy S i BMW serii 7 osiągnęły wyniki niemal o połowę niższe.
items.notes: Low-tier source, single month; 'BMW 7 Series ~half' is approximate per source. Cross-check with CPCA/insurance data.

items.headline: Willingness to pay for connected services drops to 68%
items.driver: S&P Global Mobility connected car survey: from 86% (2024) to 68% (2025); frustration with paywalled built-in hardware.
items.customer_relevance: Feature-on-demand for hardware already in the car risks backlash; bundle core comfort features into purchase price.
items.quote: from 86% in 2024 to 68% in 2025
items.notes: No 2026 edition found.

items.headline: CarPlay Ultra launches on Aston Martin; Mercedes won't use it
items.driver: Three years after announcement; Hyundai, Kia, Genesis signed up.
items.customer_relevance: Deep phone-OS takeover of all screens is available; BMW must decide how far to open its HMI to Apple.
items.quote: the Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis brands have signed up to make it compatible in their vehicles.

items.headline: CarPlay Ultra still Aston-only; Audi, Volvo, Polestar, Renault drop out
items.driver: Per FT; 13 brands incl. Porsche, Genesis, Hyundai, Ford list intent; BMW not on list.
items.customer_relevance: Most premium OEMs keep own HMI; strong standard CarPlay/Android Auto reliability matters more (see IQS 2026).
items.quote: Audi, Volvo, Polestar, and Renault have also decided against supporting CarPlay Ultra.
items.notes: BMW reportedly played down interest (secondary, not verified).
